what: curated tables (not downloaded): Russia's no-war exportable supply 2022-2026 (2021 = 1) and the infrastructure known in advance, with the sources they rest on. Primary pages (IEA, OPEC, Minenergo, government.ru, Gazprom) refuse the connection from this environment (HTTP 403 / reset, 2026-10-25); the figures were checked against the secondary reports listed, all dated before 2022 except where they report a pre-2022 plan

crude.basis: crude exports = output - refinery runs (runs flat at ~280 Mt). 2021: exports 231.6 Mt (customs), output 10.5 mb/d incl. condensate. OPEC+ (18 July 2021): +0.4 mb/d a month for the group from Aug 2021 to Sep 2022, Russia's baseline 11.0 -> 11.5 mb/d from May 2022, so Russia's required crude output rises ~0.9 mb/d from the 2021 average by Sep 2022. Energy Strategy 2035 (April 2020): output 11.15-11.25 mb/d to 2024, flat to falling to 2035. Low: output stuck at 2021 (capacity limits seen in late 2021). Central: half of the OPEC+ room is produced (about +0.45 mb/d, +4% output, +7-8% exports). High: OPEC+ path fully met, Strategy's upper bound

products.basis: refinery runs flat (~280 Mt, 2019-2021); the tax manoeuvre (2019-2024, law of Aug 2018) lowers the export of fuel oil while the damper and the 2011 modernisation agreements raise light products. Energy Strategy 2035: fuel exports 'rise considerably', fuel oil falls. Range around flat

coal.basis: Coal programme 2035 (government order 1582-r, 13 June 2020): exports 2035 +22% (conservative) to +86% (optimistic) on 2018 (bpb Russland-Analysen 386). 2018 210 Mt, 2021 ~223 Mt (BACI tonnes 222.5). From 2021 that is ~+1% a year (low) to ~+4% a year (high); the Eastern Polygon rail expansion (phase 2, 2019-2024) is the main constraint

gas_pipe.basis: pipeline gas to Europe and Turkey (Gazprom far abroad excluding China): 2021 ~175 bcm (185.1 incl. 10.4 to China). Gazprom's own 2021 guidance 175-183 bcm (April 2021). Low: 2021 level (spot sales held back in 2021). Central: 183 bcm (the top of Gazprom's 2021 target, demand-limited). High: 2019 level (~199 bcm) with Nord Stream 2 in service (the Nord Stream 2 range: on an origin basis it re-routes rather than adds; its value is the capacity to return to 2018-2019 volumes). China's pipeline gas is the Power of Siberia contract ramp (INFRA), not this index

lng.basis: 2021 LNG exports ~29.6 Mt (Yamal, Sakhalin-2, Vysotsk). Planned before 2022: Portovaya 1.5 Mt/y (2022); Arctic LNG 2, three 6.6 Mt/y trains in 2023, 2024, 2025 (Novatek, May 2021; half a year in the start year). Low: each train one year late. High: plus Yamal debottlenecking (+1 Mt/y)

Government order 1737-r of 31 Dec 2004 (ESPO); Kozmino rail-sea 15 Mt/y, Dec 2009
Russia-China loan-for-oil agreement Feb 2009, 15 Mt/y for 20 years from 2011
Rosneft-CNPC agreement June 2013: +7 Mt/y via Kazakhstan from 2014
Rosneft-CNPC 2013 contract; Mohe-Daqing second line from 1 Jan 2018 (+15 Mt/y)
Transnefteprodukt 'Sever' diesel pipeline to Primorsk (2008, 8.4 Mt; 15 Mt 2013), diverting diesel from Ventspils
Gazprom-Botas contract 1997, plateau 16 bcm/y; linear contract ramp 2003-2010
Sakhalin-2 FID May 2003, 9.6 Mt/y (13 bcm) LNG from 2009; long-term sales: Japanese buyers ~62%, KOGAS 1.5 Mt/y
Yamal LNG FID Dec 2013, 16.5 Mt/y (3 trains, 2017-2018); CNPC 3 Mt/y contract; most cargoes marketed to Europe
Gazprom-CNPC contract 21 May 2014, 38 bcm/y for 30 years; start 2 Dec 2019; ramp per Gazprom plans
Lithuanian government decision and Hoegh FSRU charter 2012; start Dec 2014, 4 bcm/y
Polskie LNG construction contract 2010; commercial operation June 2016, 5 bcm/y
Gasum/Elering FID Oct 2016 (EU CEF); start Jan 2020
LNG Hrvatska FID Jan 2019; start Jan 2021, 2.6 bcm/y
Gaz-System/Energinet FID Nov 2018; start Oct 2022, 10 bcm/y (war-time application only)
ICGB FID Dec 2019; Bulgargaz-SOCAR contract 1 bcm/y via IGB from 2021/22 (war-time application only)

sources.what: OPEC+ 19th ONOMM, 18 July 2021: +0.4 mb/d a month from Aug 2021; baselines for Saudi Arabia and Russia 11.0 -> 11.5 mb/d from May 2022

Energy Strategy of Russia to 2035 (government order 1523-r, 9 June 2020; adopted April 2020): gas output 795-820 bcm (2024), LNG 46-65 Mt (2024), 80-140 Mt (2035); oil output ~11.15-11.25 mb/d to 2024
Coal programme to 2035 (government order 1582-r, 13 June 2020): output 485 (conservative) to 668 Mt (optimistic) in 2035; exports +22% to +86% on 2018
Power of Siberia: 10.39 bcm in 2021, ~15 bcm planned for 2022, 38 bcm/y design (contract 2014)
Arctic LNG 2: 3 x 6.6 Mt/y; Novatek (May 2021) trains in 2023, 2024, 2025
Gazprom far-abroad exports 185.1 bcm in 2021 (incl. China); 2021 Europe guidance 175-183 bcm
Russia's crude exports 2021, 231.6 Mt (Russia's customs report via UN Comtrade, HS 2709 net weight)
